title: Dedicated provisioning decision matrix and handoff checklist
creator: Rohan Mehta
description: Background: As sales and CS teams sign up customers for Dedicated capacity we need an unambiguous decision matrix and an operational handoff checklist that ties: requested throughput guarantees, autoscaling policy templates, buffer sizing, billing commitments, and fleet controls. Problem: current intake is ad hoc — engineering gets partial spreadsheets and product gets high-level asks. That leads to mismatched SLAs, overprovisioned fleets, or unexpected throttling. Goal: produce a single-page decision matrix and an accompanying checklist that can be used by sales/CS/solutions/product to generate an actionable provisioning request that engineering can implement with minimal back-and-forth. Scope: only Dedicated (reserved) offerings — includes burst policies, soft guarantees, early-decommit rules, and runbook links. Non-goal: changing pricing models or the console UI surface (those will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix (PDF and markdown) maps customer throughput/latency needs to a recommended capacity profile and an autoscale template
Handoff checklist items cover: quota spec, expected traffic patterns, test probes, canary window, SLO targets, billing commit, and rollback triggers
Engineering sign-off on implementability (PR with example FleetConfig) and no outstanding blockers
Two runbook links created: provisioning-runbook and post-provisioning-observability-checklist
Train-the-trainer session scheduled for Sales and CS with slide deck and Q&A notes
rollout_plan: Draft matrix and checklist (PM owner) — 1 week
Sync with runtime eng to map FleetConfig fields to matrix outputs — 3 days
Pilot with 2 active customers (small and medium) — 2 weeks
Iterate based on pilot feedback and finalize artifacts — 1 week
Publish to internal playbook and run training session — 3 days
metrics: Time from intake to provisioned capacity (target <= 5 business days)
Post-provision latency SLO misses in first 72h (target < 1%)
risks: Under-specified traffic patterns causing incorrect buffer sizing
Edge-case models with bursty token patterns might need custom kernel selection — not covered by template
Billing/legal requirements for some enterprise deals may require non-standard guardrails
If engineering FleetConfig surface changes, matrix mappings must be updated
